extracted.intended_audience: rOpenSci editors or maintainers recruiting reviewers for package peer review
extracted.subtask_description: An e-mail template and associated expectations for editors inviting potential reviewers to perform open peer review of an R package on behalf of rOpenSci. Specifies required invitation content, timelines, conduct expectations, and available reviewer supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation content completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The invitation should name the reviewer, identify the editor, briefly introduce the package (package name, author(s), what it does), provide the GitHub repository link, and link to the onboarding issue for the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template includes placeholders: [REVIEWER], [EDITOR], [PACKAGE], [AUTHOR(S)], [FUNCTION], [REPO LINK], [ONBOARDING ISSUE]. Provide these details so the reviewer can find the package and the review thread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Request that reviewers complete reviews in three weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template states: 'If you accept, note that we ask reviewers to complete reviews in three weeks. (We’ve found it takes a similar amount of time to review a package as an academic paper.)' Use the three-week deadline as the expected turnaround.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews are conducted openly via GitHub.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The email directs reviewers to the GitHub onboarding issue and states: 'We conduct our open review process via GitHub as well, here: [ONBOARDING ISSUE]'. Ensure reviewers know the review will be public on GitHub.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reviewer resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Point reviewers to the reviewers guide, packaging guide, and a reviewer template to support conducting the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template links: reviewers guide (details what we look for and example reviews), packaging guide (standards), and reviewer template (for use). Encourage reviewers to consult these resources before and during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest check
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must ensure they do not have a conflict of interest preventing them from reviewing the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Template instructs: 'Please make sure you do not have a conflict of interest (https://devguide.ropensci.org/policies.html#coi) preventing you from reviewing this package.' If a COI exists, decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and conduct expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be open, non-adversarial, and focused on improving software quality; reviewers should be respectful and kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The email emphasizes community values: 'rOpenSci’s community is our best asset. We aim for reviews to be open, non-adversarial, and focused on improving software quality. Be respectful and kind!' It also points to the code of conduct (https://ropensci.org/code-of-conduct/).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship availability for first-time reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reviewer requested mentorship, the editor may act as a resource, offering email/Slack support, draft feedback, and optional videocalls to walk through the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template includes an optional mentorship paragraph: the editor can provide Slack access, review draft reviews, answer questions, and schedule brief videocalls. Use these supports for first reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response expectation and alternate suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask the invited reviewer to reply within one week; if unable to review, request suggestions for alternate reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template states: 'Are you able to review? If you can not, suggestions for alternate reviewers are always helpful. If I don't hear from you within a week, I will assume you are unable to review at this time.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reviewer template
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are encouraged (and provided) to use the rOpenSci reviewer template when writing their review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invitation links to the reviewer template (https://devguide.ropensci.org/reviewtemplate.html) and notes it is provided 'for you to use.' This helps standardize reviews.
